title: This Long-Awaited Feature Is Finally Coming to the Apple Watch
description: Apple has finally figured out we want to know our step count.
fullText:
We expect fitness wearables to count our steps—an idea that Fitbit borrowed from pedometers forever ago. In recent years even Oura and Whoop have added step tracking. But the Apple Watch has never made it easy to see your step count, even though it’s been keeping track in the background all along. Apple is finally changing that.

On the product pages for the Series 12 and the Apple Watch Ultra, Apple boasts that the new watches give you a more accurate step count—interesting, because step count hasn’t been a selling point in the past. And then comes the big news: “And now you can more easily check your step count, right from your watch face.”

So far, it has been frustratingly difficult to get a step count on your watch. You would think you could easily add that number to a watch complication (a complication being a mini data field for the watch face), but nope—if you want a little counter of your steps on the watch face, you have to install a third-party app to provide that.

I kind of understand why: Apple wanted to set itself apart from the Fitbits of the world. You’re supposed to close your rings, and rings are based on movement, exercise, and stand hours. I can imagine somebody at Apple saying “no, step counting is dumb” and they were arguably right. But the idea has stuck in the public consciousness; we now expect step counts, and Apple is finally going to deliver.

First of all, the Apple Watch already counts your steps. You can see your step count by going to the Health app on your phone and searching for Steps. Scroll to the bottom of the Steps screen and tap Add to Pinned. Now it will be the first thing you see when you open the Health app. (Surprised the Health app can do this? You have no idea of the hidden gems in that thing.)

To get a step count on your Apple Watch right now, without upgrading anything, you’ll need to install a step counter app. Duffy is a popular (free) one; there are plenty of others out there, so choose one you like. These apps typically provide a complication, so you can add your step count to your favorite watch face.

But what about taking advantage of Apple’s new embrace of the step count? Apple says the feature will be available on the Series 12 and Ultra 4 watches. That said, this seems like a very simple software change, so I’d bet money that step count will become available in WatchOS 27, which is due out any day now, and which will run on Series 9 and newer, Ultra 2 and newer, and the SE 3. I’m currently using the WatchOS 27 public beta, and there’s no step count feature yet, but I’m watching for it.

I also spied step counts in Apple’s screenshots of its upcoming redesign of the Health app. This is an app that lives on your phone, and in the screenshot there was a little tile with your Apple Watch rings, and underneath the rings, the step count. Apple says the Health app redesign will be available on devices that support Apple Intelligence, which means the iPhone 15 Pro and newer.

Once you have the feature on your watch, it looks like step counts will be available on the cards you see when you swipe up from the main watch face. Currently you can pin a card there with your step distance for the day (I’ve covered 0.65 miles between waking up and making my way to my home office) but steps aren’t available there yet.

title: 10 Hacks Every Google Photos User Should Know
description: You can save yourself a lot of Google Photos storage with these hacks.
fullText:
Google Photos doesn't have to be one of those things that you set up and forget. Despite its initial simplicity, Google Photos is full of settings and features you can configure to make the app work better for you. With these hacks, you can manage a massive photo library, reduce cloud storage, hide pictures of your ex, and disable AI in search.

If you feel like you’re going to run out of cloud storage space, and you don’t care about backing up photos and videos at the best quality possible, try Google’s Storage saver mode. When backing up, it automatically scales down photos and videos to help you save cloud storage space at a respectable quality level. Photos get scaled down to 16MP, and videos stay at 1080p. This only works for new uploads, though, so the sooner you enable this feature, the better off you’ll be. Go to Settings > Backup > Photo and Video Quality and switch to Storage Saver.

Google Photos' Memories feature surfaces old photos and videos, and stitches them together in slideshows and videos. But this can also backfire if it shows you photos of people (say, an ex) you'd rather not see randomly in notifications when you're trying to work. Memories is thankfully highly customizable. You can tell Google Photos to show you more photos of your partner, kids, or pets, and ask it to show fewer photos of specific people. You can even block people from ever surfacing in suggestions. Go to Photos settings > Preferences > Memories > Hide Faces. Then, choose the faces that you want to block.

You can use the Locked Folder in Google Photos to save sensitive photos or documents in a secure folder. Only a PIN or biometrics can get you through. But by default, the Locked Folder contents are local-only. Even if your entire Google Photos library is backed up, you might lose all that secured media if you lose your phone.

There is a hidden setting that does let you back up and sync locked photos securely. Even after they are synced to the cloud and other devices, they will continue to stay in the Locked Folder. If it's not already set up, go to the Collections tab, swipe all the way to the bottom, and choose Locked Folder. During setup, you can enable the cloud backup feature. Alternatively, open the Locked Folder, tap the Cloud icon on the top toolbar, and enable Back up Locked Folder.

The days of unlimited media backup on Google Photos are long gone. If you’re on the free 15GB Google plan, you might run out of storage entirely by backing up your entire photo library—which then leads to interruptions in services like Gmail and Google Drive. If you want to make do with the free storage that you have (or you don’t want to upgrade to a more expensive plan), try "Recover Storage" first. It sifts through the photos and videos that you've already uploaded and compresses them to the same quality as the Storage Saver mode I talked about above. For this to work, you'll need to visit the Google Photos website. From the sidebar, choose Storage, and click Learn More under Recover Storage. Tick the I Understand checkbox and click Compress existing photos & videos to get started.

Google Photos on Android can go beyond backing up your camera roll. Because Google Photos has direct access to the Android file system, it can upload photos and videos from any folder. This includes the Downloads folder for Chrome, or WhatsApp’s media folder. That said, you should audit exactly which folders are being uploaded. You might want it to upload photos from the Downloads folder, but exclude WhatsApp media (which is already uploaded to Google Drive, if you have online backup enabled). From Photos Settings, go to Backup Settings > Default backup > Device folders, choose the folders you want to back up, and deselect ones you want to skip.

Google Photos has a storage management tool that can help you get rid of photos and videos that are unnecessarily taking up too much space on your plan. From Photos settings, go to Backup > Manage storage. This opens up the Google One storage management screen where you can get rid of large attachments and files as well. But what I find more interesting is the Google Photos option in the "Clean up by service" section. Here, Google will intelligently suggest photos and videos to delete, categorized in tabs on top. This includes large video files, duplicate photos, screenshots that you don’t need, and more. Choose the photos you want to delete, and then tap Delete at the top.

If you’re purging your Google Photos library to reclaim some space, you might be stumped. You just deleted a bunch of photos and videos, but your cloud storage numbers haven't dropped. That’s because deleting a photo or video doesn’t actually remove it from your account, at least not yet. Google stores media for up to 30 days, in case you want to retrieve it later on. To completely get rid of deleted media, scroll to the bottom, find the Collections section, and choose Trash (or Bin). Here, tap the three-dot menu button, choose Empty Bin, and confirm using the Delete Permanently option.

Google is trying to stuff AI editing features and Gemini into the Google Photos app. Most of it lives in the Create tab, which is easy enough to ignore. But Ask Photos is not. When you go to Search, it now integrates AI search directly into the results. This means that quickly searching for photos of a location, person, or a stored album takes a bit more time, and it might get influenced by an AI suggestion. Thankfully, there is a toggle that removes all the AI features from Search. Go to Photos Settings > Preferences > Gemini features in Photos and disable the Ask Photos feature. And while you’re here, you can choose to disable all Gemini features in Google Photos as well.

Google offers a service called Google Takeout, where you can download an offline copy of all the data that Google has, including all your emails, files, and photos. Offline backups should be a part of every cohesive backup strategy, which makes Takeout a useful feature. But there’s always been an issue with Takeout: Every time you make a request, the feature downloads all the data, even if you only wanted to see what was new.

Now, Google has introduced incremental exports. This means that only data created since the last export will be downloaded. Go to the Google Takeout website, sign in with your account, and only select Google Photos from the list. Then, choose the albums and media to export and hit Next. In the Frequency section, choose the Export every month for 1 year, or the Export every 2 months for 1 year option. Make sure to switch to the Only new and updated items option to turn on the incremental feature.

If you’re paying for the $20 per month Google AI Pro plan, you get 5TB of cloud storage space included in the price. This is great for backing up your photo library and all the files on your computer. If you’re a photo or video professional, or you just like backing up photos via your Mac (after editing them), Google used to have a perfect solution with its Google Photos desktop backup. It would monitor a folder and automatically upload new items to the cloud. Sadly, that feature is no longer available.

If you want the feature, switch to Amazon Photos on your computer instead. The dedicated desktop app uploads photos and videos from any folder, in the background. If you have Amazon Prime, you can upload unlimited photos for free, as well as 5GB of videos.

title: Yes, the Apple Watch's New Audio Intelligence Features Really Are Always Listening to You
description: If you think that sounds like a privacy nightmare, you're not wrong.
fullText:
During its Sept. 9 keynote, Apple announced the Apple Watch Series 12 and the Ultra 4, both of which will come with a feature that passively listens to your audio conversations all day and can summarize them for you on demand. It's part of a collection of features called "Audio Intelligence," but the two key features to consider here are:

Live Rewind: If you double-press the Digital Crown on your Apple Watch, it will pull up a text snippet of your conversation over the last fifteen seconds.

Siri Recaps: Your watch listens to your conversations and generates an AI summary of any of your transcribed audio at the end of each day.

At first glance, the basic concept seems like a privacy nightmare, but Apple has put some safeguards in place to help people feel more comfortable with this feature: The audio that is captured is never recorded or stored, and never leaves your device; it is essentially deleted immediately and in real time from local storage; only a truncated version is uploaded to Apple Private Cloud Compute servers for AI processing, and the resulting transcript that is delivered to you is end-to-end encrypted.

Still, there are some potential privacy concerns worth considering, especially since you'll essentially be subjecting everyone around you to using it without their consent.

Series 12 and Ultra 4 watches run on an S11 chip with a Secure Exclave feature, a partitioned local storage compartment that even the operating system cannot access. When your Apple Watch picks up ambient audio, it is sent straight into this protected buffer, where it is encrypted, then sent over to a matching Secure Enclave on your paired iPhone.

From there, your iPhone transcribes it locally using an on-device AI model to create a summarized version that’s half the length of the actual audio, removing everything but the essentials, and stripping out any identifying information. After the audio data is overwritten, the transcript is sent to Apple's Private Cloud Compute along with some generic metadata, like a rough location and timestamps.

None of the audio data is tied to your Apple ID once it reaches the servers at this stage. Apple uses a third-party relay to conceal your IP address while uploading the data to Private Cloud Compute, so not even their employees can identify you from your device. While in the Private Cloud Compute servers, your audio data gets summarized by Siri AI. This is how you end up with daily text summaries of your audio, provided you opt into Siri Recap. Siri Recap summaries are auto-deleted every seven days unless you choose to save them individually.

All of this might seem perfectly secure, but here comes the risky part: If you choose to save a conversation summary with Siri Recap, that data is uploaded to your iCloud storage and can even be saved in apps like Apple Notes or Journal. Server-level data breaches at companies like Apple are rare, but account-level hacks happen more often than you might think: 900,000 compromised iCloud logins were found sitting on a public server after a data leak just this January.

If someone manages to hack into your Apple ID or access your unsecured iPhone, they might be able to view all your saved conversation summaries from a single place. And it’s not just the potential data breach that should scare you, but all the associated privacy concerns.

Apple has spent a lot of time thinking through ways to protect its customers when they use the Audio Intelligence feature, but none of these protections extend to other people who might be sitting across the table or in the same room as you.

To its credit, Apple has added an audio chime and a brief visual cue that plays on your watch whenever the Live Rewind feature is triggered. This is intended to inform people around you that they are being listened to. Live Rewind also doesn’t identify speakers, so it won’t name or otherwise identify the person speaking in the transcriptions or summaries—but none of that actually prevents people from being eavesdropped on without their explicit consent.

Siri Recap’s implementation is arguably even worse. It has no audio or visual cues to indicate that it’s running, so no one knows that they are being surveilled if you enable this feature. Apple’s privacy documentation is visibly scarce when it comes to the issue of consent, apart from a vague warning on the product pages that advises you to “be mindful of those around you.”

This is a potential concern not just for other people who might worry about being spied on every time they see an Apple Watch, but also Apple Watch users themselves, if they are in a region where local laws require consent before recording audio: Some 12 U.S. states have explicit all-party consent laws that forbid undisclosed recordings, while outside the U.S., many E.U. countries have instituted similar requirements; the E.U.'s GDPR also prohibits recordings containing personally identifiable information without disclosure.

Using an Apple Watch with the Audio Intelligence feature enabled might sound like it would put you in violation of these laws, but at this point, it seems the device operates in a bit of a grey area—as Apple's privacy documentation notes:

Audio Intelligence features do not create audio recordings that can be accessedby the operating system, apps, the user, or Apple. There is no recording to share,forward, or produce if requested by any party, because no recording exists.

The Secure Exclave buffer where the audio is initially processed is "a continuously overwritten stream that exists only within the protected hardware and never creates an audio recording," Apple says, meaning no one needs to consent to being recorded. In theory. But that Apple felt the need to go into great detail to explain how the feature technically doesn't violate any privacy laws probably doesn't make it feel any less dystopian to those inclined to view it that way.

Given all the potential security concerns, it’s a good thing that Apple has at least made its Audio Intelligence features opt-in only. They won’t be enabled by default on your new Apple Watch, and you can choose to enable or disable individual features as you choose to. Here's what to look for:

Sound Recognition: Open the Settings app on your iPhone. Navigate to Accessibility > Sound & Name Recognition > Sound Recognition. Here you can toggle the “Detect using Apple Watch” option on or off.

Music Recognition: Open the Settings app directly on your Apple Watch. Tap on Smart Stack. Switch "Music Detection" on or off per your needs.

Live Rewind: Open the Watch app on your iPhone. Go to Siri > Live Rewind. You can choose to enable or disable “Double Click Digital Crown” to control this feature.

Siri Recap: Again on the Watch app on your iPhone, go to Siri > Siri Recap. You can enable or disable the feature here, or even set an autorun schedule for it if you like. Siri Recap can also be switched on and off by flipping a single toggle in your Control Center.

title: If You Loved 'The Office,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next
description: Missing the Scranton gang at Dunder Mifflin? There’s one movie that you absolutely have to watch.
fullText:
Since ending its nine-season run in 2013, The Office has only grown more powerful. Thanks to endless re-runs and availability on streaming platforms, the series has evolved into the glue that holds society together—no matter who you are, you’ve watched The Office (probably more than once, with the exception of “Scott’s Tots,” which is simply too cringey (though hilarious!) for anyone to experience twice). If you just finished your sixth re-watch and you’ve watched all the recommended streamalike series, it’s time to watch David Brent: Life on the Road.

If you’re a huge fan of The Office, you’ve almost certainly watched the original UK version created by Rickey Gervais. The original series has a different vibe than the American version, of course, but all the pieces are there—especially Gervais’s performance as David Brent, who was a slightly meaner Michael Scott.

That’s what makes David Brent: Life on the Road a must-watch for Office fans. It picks up Brent’s story after the series’ end and digs deep into his character. No longer the boss, Brent is working as a sales rep—and finds himself in the same position his employees once did, miserable in his work and treated poorly by many of his co-workers. Instead of inspiring some self-reflection, however, Brent decides to make a desperate stab at music stardom, cleaning out his retirement funds to hire a band and go on a short tour during his vacation.

There’s very little office in David Brent: Life on the Road, but the film has the same cringe-comedy chops you love about the series. Brent is as bombastic, un-self-aware, and weirdly overconfident as ever when the story kicks off, but—just like Michael in the U.S. series—is slowly humanized over the course of the story, learning how to make real human connections. Along the way, there’s plenty of awkward comedy and hilarious moments, all done in the same mockumentary style of both the original show and the American adaptation. If you’re looking for something similar to bridge the gap to your next re-watch of the show, this is the perfect choice. Stream David Brent: Life on the Road on Netflix.

If that just made you want to watch more office-based comedies or mockumentaries that do cringe comedy well, never fear: Here are a few more movies fans of The Office will love.

No recent comedy captures the slow, grinding indignities of working life like Office Space. If you love how The Office riffs on the personalities and petty squabbles between co-workers that come to dominate our 9-to-5 existences, this story of a man who decides his job just doesn’t matter (and who gets swept up in a ludicrous crime scheme that’s ripped off of Superman 3, of all things) is an ideal choice. It digs into what we sell to our employers, the rage that working for a living can inspire (this scene connects with literally everyone who watches it), and the hilarious absurdity of office life. Rent Office Space on Prime Video.

Office culture and its warping effect on human nature has been a comedic subject for a long time, and this peak Billy Wilder film from 1960 is still relatable today. Jack Lemmon plays a put-upon, ambitious office clerk at an enormous insurance company that allows executives to use his bachelor pad as a trysting place for their office affairs, hoping to ingratiate himself. It’s as much a satire of corporate culture as it is a love story, and modern-day Office fans will find a lot of the jokes still land today. Stream The Apartment on Kanopy or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Clockwatchers offers a different kind of humor and explores a kind of working experience that doesn’t really exist anymore—that of long-term temp workers. But if your favorite part of The Office is the way it skewers work culture and office dynamics, this is your jam. Toni Colette plays Iris, a young woman who starts a temp gig at a mid-size financial company. She hooks up with the other temps (including a typically marvelous Parker Posey and Lisa Kudrow) and learns the ins and outs of this stressful, darkly funny office. Anyone trapped in a dead-end job will understand the peculiar madness that sets in—the same madness that drives the funny core of this movie. Stream Clockwatchers on Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Are your favorite episodes of The Office the ones where normal order breaks down and chaos invades, like the Christmas party episode, the fire drill cold open, or the office Olympics?. Check out Office Christmas Party. A struggling office is ordered to cancel bonuses and its holiday party, but the CTO and branch manager forge ahead with the party in an effort to land a big client. The phrase “chaos ensues” does not even begin to sum up the events that follow, including copious property damage, arrests, and several hospitalizations. If Dwight and Jim’s prank wars and Michael’s tendency to overdo everything were the best parts of the show for you, you’ll dig this. Stream Office Christmas Party on Paramount+ or rent it on Prime Video.

If you’re a sucker for the “mockumentary” format The Office perfected, Waiting for Guffman is the perfect choice. The story of a community theater group planning a show for the town’s 150th anniversary, led by intense director Corky St. Clair (Christopher Guest). It captures Michael Scott’s oblivious approach to leading a team and his improvisational comedy skills as the weirdos who populate the community of Blaine, Missouri come together to put on a show that is a lot more memorable than it is good. Rent Waiting for Guffman on Prime Video.

title: Austrian woman dies after alleged sexual abuse by husband in case local media dubs ‘Pelicot 2.0’
description: An Austrian woman died after her husband injured and sexually abused her while she was “extremely intoxicated,” prosecutors say, in a case that local media are comparing to that of Frenchwoman Gisèle ...
fullText:
An Austrian woman died after her husband injured and sexually abused her while she was "extremely intoxicated," prosecutors say, in a case that local media are comparing to that of Frenchwoman Gisèle Pelicot.

Prosecutors in the Austrian city of Wels told CNN the woman was "defenseless" in her condition and that another man confessed to sexually abusing the woman, including on the night that she died.

They are also investigating whether other men may have also sexually abused the woman, potentially in exchange for payment, they said.

Austrian media have dubbed the case "Pelicot 2.0," drawing comparisons to Gisèle Pelicot, whose former husband Dominique Pelicot was convicted of aggravated rape after drugging her for years and recruiting dozens of strangers to rape her while she was unconscious.

Prosecutors said reports in the local press of a so called wider "rape network" cannot yet be confirmed but remain under investigation.

The victim was found severely injured and bleeding at her home in Marchtrenk, near Wels in Upper Austria, on June 26, according to prosecutors. Paramedics pronounced her dead at the scene and an autopsy was ordered.

Prosecutors told CNN that the husband initially said her death had been part of an "accident" during sex. But the victim's injuries, they said, "indicate violence."

Her death was first reported in the summer by Austria Press Agency but details of the investigation have only recently emerged.

Authorities said the 51-year-old husband and the second man, who is also 51 and was arrested last month, are now in custody. Prosecutors said only the husband has been linked to the act that caused her death.

The husband has declined to comment on the allegations. He is being investigated over allegations of abuse of a defenseless or impaired person resulting in death, an offense carrying a potential sentence of 10 to 20 years in prison or life.

He could ultimately face a murder charge, depending on what investigators are able to establish about his intent.

Prosecutors said no money is believed to have changed hands between the husband and the second man currently in custody.

The Wels Public Prosecutor's Office told CNN the investigation is ongoing and declined to provide further details about the alleged acts, citing respect for the victim and investigative considerations.

CNN's Caroline Baum contributed to this report

title: Brilliant Lowry surges clear as McIlroy struggles
description: Shane Lowry cards a course-record 62 to take control of the Irish Open as putting woes prevent defending champion Rory McIlroy from making a second-round charge in Doonbeg.
fullText:
Irish Open, second-round leaderboard

-11 S Lowry (Ire); -8 H Li (Chn), N Norgaard (Den), J Skov Olesen (Den); -5 E Ferguson (Sco), J Niemann (Chi), K Kobori (NZ), N Hojgaard (Den), T McKibbin (NI); -4 A Sullivan (Eng), P Reed (USA), R Neergaard-Petersen (Den), J Dantrop (Swe)

Selected others: -3 J Rahm (Spa), R MacIntyre (Sco); -2 R McIlroy (NI); -1 A Fitzpatrick (Eng); E L Donald (Eng), S Garcia (Spa); +1 B Koepka (USA), S Straka (Aut)

Shane Lowry carded a course-record 62 to take control of the Irish Open as putting woes prevented defending champion Rory McIlroy from making a second-round charge at Doonbeg.

Irishman Lowry, who won his national title as an amateur in 2009, made six birdies in the space of seven holes on his front nine to surge clear in more favourable conditions after Thursday's heavy wind and rain.

Three more birdies - and a bogey on 13 - followed as the 39-year-old established a three-shot lead over China's Li Haotong and the Danish pair of Jacob Skov Olesen and Niklas Norgaard Moller at Trump International Golf Links in County Clare on the west coast of the Republic of Ireland.

"It was real fun out there. I got off to a nice start and then I just kept going," said Lowry, who is playing his first tournament since failing to make the final two PGA Tour play-off events.

"I felt great out there. Just kept my foot on the gas and tried to keep hitting good shots and keep holing putts and it was a nice day."

Irish Open second round as it happened - Lowry breaks course record

With all parts of his game operating efficiently, Lowry started with two pars before reeling off a hat-trick of birdies from the third.

After a par on the sixth, the 2019 Open champion drained a 24-foot putt for a birdie two on the next and closed out his front nine with two more birdies to turn in six-under 30.

Lowry, who has not won an individual title in four years, scrambled for a par five at 10 when he hacked out of long rough before holing a 10-footer.

Birdies at 11 and 12 ignited hopes of a 59 at the par-70 venue before a sloppy bogey on 13 when he three-putted from 18 feet.

But the world number 53, who attracted large galleries around the spectacular links course, rolled in a 19-footer for birdie at 15 to return to -11 before finishing with three pars.

"I thought about it," Lowry, who has not returned a top-20 finish since February, said when asked if a sub-60 round entered his mind.

"Yeah, I did think about it until I three-putted 13. No, I did have a little laugh. Out in 30 and the back nine is only 34, so, yeah, you do kind of think about it a little bit."

He added: "I know I made a little mistake on 13, but I think I did a good job after that of playing the rest of the round really well and giving myself a couple of chances on the way in."

While Lowry prospered in more benign conditions, his good friend and Ryder Cup team-mate McIlroy failed to climb the leaderboard as he finished the day nine shots back and in a tie for 21st place.

Six-time major winner McIlroy, who is chasing a third Irish Open triumph, was even par for his round before a stunning fairway metal from 267 yards to two feet set up an eagle three at the eighth.

That moment of brilliance failed to ignite McIlroy's challenge, however, as he bogeyed the 11th and missed a series of birdie putts before sinking a 40-footer to pick up a shot at the 17th.

Northern Ireland's McIlroy looked set for a birdie-birdie finish after firing his approach at the final hole to four feet, but he took three putts to drop a shot and card a second consecutive 69.

"I just didn't have it on the greens. I really struggled to read them," said McIlroy.

He added: "It's been a tough one on the greens the last two days. But tee to green I've actually been pretty happy with how everything else is. I just need to try to hole a few more over the weekend."

Li, Norgaard and Olesen established themselves as Lowry's closest challengers.

Li, who finished tied fourth in last year's Open Championship at Royal Portrush, carded seven birdies, an eagle and two bogeys to shoot 63, while Olesen mixed seven birdies with a single bogey in a 64.

In the late wave, Norgaard matched his compatriot's 64 with a bogey-free round.

Northern Ireland's Tom McKibbin shaved a shot off his opening 68 to reach five under, a group which includes Scotland's Ewen Ferguson (66) and 2024 winner Rasmus Hojgaard (63).

Playing with McIlroy, Scotland's Robert MacIntyre bounced back from an opening 72 with a fine 65 to sit eight shots back alongside two-time winner Jon Rahm, who recorded four birdies in a 67.

Race to Dubai leader and 2018 Masters winner Patrick Reed is one shot better off on four under, but five-time major champion Brooks Koepka needed a birdie on 18 to shoot 66 and sneak inside the cut line on one over.

Home favourites Seamus Power (+4) and Padraig Harrington (+8), as well as Tyrrell Hatton (+8) are among those who will not make the weekend.

Irish Open will feel 'different' with Trump visit

title: Liverpool unveil memorials for former manager Beard
description: Liverpool have unveiled permanent memorials at their training ground and outside Anfield in tribute to former women's team manager Matt Beard.
fullText:
Liverpool have unveiled permanent memorials outside Anfield and at their training ground in tribute to former women's team manager Matt Beard.

He died on 20 September, 2025, aged 47, and having been in charge from 2012 to 2015 and again from 2021 to 2025.

Under his management Liverpool won back-to-back Women's Super League titles in 2013 and 2014, before securing promotion back to the WSL in 2022 by winning the FA Women's Championship title.

Beard was twice named WSL manager of the season, and inducted into the WSL Hall of Fame earlier this year.

Players, staff and Beard's family attended a private ceremony at the club's Melwood training ground on Friday where a memorial garden in his name was unveiled.

A commemorative tree was also planted in his honour on 97 Avenue outside Anfield Stadium.

Liverpool's home Premier League match against Fulham on Saturday will be dedicated to the league's Together Against Suicide initiative, which raises awareness of suicide prevention and the support available.

The campaign runs between 4 and 14 September to encourage conversations around suicide prevention and help reduce the stigma about people seeking support.

A group of Reds supporters will also raise money for men's suicide prevention charity Andy's Man Club by walking from Melwood to the Brewdog Stadium in St Helens - Liverpool Women's home ground - before Sunday's WSL match against Tottenham.

Last September the Liverpool FC Foundation launched its Kicking Off Conversations Hub to offer specialist support to fans.

title: Swans winger Inoussa joins Gornik Zabrze on loan
description: Swansea City winger Zeidane Inoussa joins Polish club Gornik Zabrze on loan for the remainder of the season.
fullText:
Swansea City winger Zeidane Inoussa has joined Polish top-flight club Gornik Zabrze on loan for the remainder of the season.

The deal comes after the 24-year-old was omitted from Swansea's English Football League (EFL) squad list.

Inoussa came close to joining Portsmouth on English football's transfer deadline day earlier this month and was also linked with a loan move to Croatian side Osijek this week.

Inoussa is under contract at Swansea until 2030 and the Championship club have an option to recall him in January.

"We hope he makes an impact [at Gornik Zabrze]," said Swansea head coach Vitor Matos.

"He's a wonderful kid, a really good professional. He just needs game-time and consistency in playing.

"I think that's what he wants as well so it's a good option in terms of finding that. We are here for him and hopefully everything goes right."

The Swans paid a significant fee to sign Inoussa from BK Hacken in the summer of 2025, but the former Sweden Under-21s international has had a limited impact in the Championship.

Inoussa scored once in 29 Swansea appearances last season, and did not feature after January due to a stress fracture in his back.

With competition in Matos' squad fierce for game-time out wide, Inoussa has not been involved in a matchday squad in 2026-27.

title: Tough chats and Three Peaks - Durham's road to the title
description: Head coach Ryan Campbell explains how Durham turned a winter of soul-searching into a successful summer in Division Two.
fullText:
After a winter of soul-searching and recriminations off the cricket field, Durham have produced a summer of dominance on it to win the County Championship Division Two title at a canter.

The recriminations came from a horrendous Headingley Saturday 12 months ago. Needing to bat out a possible 89 overs to avoid relegation, Durham were skittled for just 85 by Yorkshire as they went down by a single point to hand a huge reprieve to Hampshire.

A season which had begun with positive chat about challenging to win the Championship had ended in the worst possible manner.

Hard conversations were needed behind closed doors about what went wrong, but the north-east county carried that anger with them to correct their mistakes and get back to the top division at the earliest possible opportunity thanks to a 93-run win over Middlesex.

"Twelve months is a long time in cricket, a long time in sport," head coach Ryan Campbell told BBC's Test Match Special.

"We sat there in this club and did not panic. We worked through a few issues, we had some heated debates about a few things, the players took on board what we wanted to change and how we wanted to do things, so I'm really grateful to be back here and win the thing."

There was no question about the quality within Durham's ranks but the questions were about temperament and their ability to cope when put under pressure.

As such, Western Australian Campbell decided that it was time to get tough during the off-season and so the squad embarked upon the challenge of scaling Britain's three highest peaks - Ben Nevis, Scafell Pike and Snowdon - within 24 hours.

"Basically we wanted to test the players mentally and put them in situations they didn't really enjoy," he said.

Campbell jokingly recalls the adventure as "absolute torture", but the shared experience of facing up to adversity was one for everyone's memory banks.

After a poor time on the field, the other kneejerk reaction can be to change everything, but the director of cricket Marcus North, head coach Campbell and crucially captain Alex Lees all stayed in post.

However, Campbell was firm in his belief in giving Lees more backing following a tough first year in the post after taking over from Scott Borthwick.

"It's very easy to throw blame at the leaders when things are not going so well," he said. "But I felt that we hadn't supported him enough.

"We needed to create an extra layer for him, so Alex wasn't taking on everything all day, every day. We put a leadership group together, which has worked out extremely well for us. That took a lot of pressure off Alex.

"We believe we have a very talented squad with batting and bowling, which everyone talks about. We had to get the best out of it but to come back the way we have, which has been pretty brutal at times, has been pretty pleasing to watch."

After the capitulation at Headingley on the final afternoon of last season, final-day run chases in key home games with Lancashire and Northamptonshire, of 336 and 296 respectively, showed that Durham had learned the lessons of going after a game rather than sinking into their shells.

Those were probably the most dramatic of their nine wins in a season in which they have dominated the division.

David Bedingham was the top run-scorer with 1,029 runs before he headed home to South Africa, while Matthew Potts' 58 wickets have him as the leading wicket-taker in county cricket this summer.

Emilio Gay hit three centuries in six matches before England came calling, while young batter Ben McKinney has also hit three big hundreds to demonstrate his potential.

Ben Raine has been his usual consistent self as a fine county performer and left-arm spinner Callum Parkinson has come to the fore since the Championship resumed after the summer break.

England drop Carse after nightclub incident

Stokes returns to Durham training after England omission

Drama and distraction has also circled around the club during the summer. Ben Stokes' suspension from the England team for a Test in June, before his return and then eventual retirement from Test cricket and the England captaincy, created a circus.

Events in Derby city centre involving Brydon Carse following a win away to Derbyshire last month also provided unwelcome headlines.

Their absences from England have been Durham's gain and Campbell has been happy to give players a platform to relax and perform, with Carse taking nine wickets in the title-clinching win over Middlesex.

"In a perfect world, you don't want any distractions," said the head coach. "But a sports team isn't a perfect world.

"We feel like we're a family here at Durham and when one of our family is in trouble, we put the wagons around and embrace them.

"Ben and Brydon, at the minute, they're here and they're happy. We'll always support them.

"We didn't know Ben was going to retire from Test cricket, we didn't know Brydon was going to be left out of the one-day squad. They've been added bonuses, but we've embraced them and they've embraced us back."

title: Dictator meme shows lack of human awareness - Mbappe
description: Kylian Mbappe criticises a viral meme which superimposes his face on the body of a dictator, saying it shows "a lack of political and human awareness".
fullText:
Kylian Mbappe has criticised a viral meme which superimposes his face on the body of a dictator, saying it shows "a lack of political and human awareness".

The Real Madrid and France forward, 27, said he understood there was a "funny side" to the AI-generated meme, but that it downplayed serious issues.

It is seemingly used by some fans on social media to reflect the way Mbappe dominates matches, while others have suggested it refers to his influence at clubs.

Speaking in an interview with France Football, external, Mbappe said: "There's a funny side to it because you can sense that, for some people, it's good natured.

"Then there's a side that's a bit less funny, because we know the damage people like that have caused throughout history.

"Being compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions upon millions of people miserable... I don't think I've done that in my life.

"On one hand, I know it's done lightheartedly and doesn't go that far, but it sometimes reveals a lack of political and human awareness among people."

Mbappe also referenced the "Mobut" nickname he was called by France team-mate Ousmane Dembele during the 2026 World Cup.

That nickname comes from Mobutu Sese Seko, the dictator who ruled the Democratic Republic of Congo - formerly Zaire - for three decades.

"Ousmane, that's a different thing. He took that from social media. He's just having a laugh," Mbappe said.

title: Dunbar wins stage as Mas maintains lead in Vuelta
description: Ireland's Eddie Dunbar wins the 19th stage of the Vuelta a Espana as Spain's Enric Mas maintains his overall lead with two stages remaining.
fullText:
Ireland's Eddie Dunbar won the 19th stage of the Vuelta a Espana as Spain's Enric Mas maintained his overall lead with two stages remaining.

Friday's stage was a hilly slog of 210.8km from Velez-Malaga to Penas Blancas, with Dunbar, 30, catching and passing Santiago Buitrago 300 metres from the finish.

Both were part of a four-man breakaway and the Colombian, the King of the Mountains leader, attacked with two kilometres to go.

Dunbar did not respond initially but the Pinarello-Q36.5 rider timed his counter-attack perfectly to cross the line 14 seconds before Buitrago, with his British team-mate Thomas Gloag in third.

Four-time Vuelta winner Primoz Roglic closed the gap on race leader Mas by 33 seconds during Thursday's time trial, but the Movistar rider held on to his lead despite general classification rivals Roglic and Richard Carapaz trying to increase the pace on the 18km climb to the finish.

Britain's Oscar Onley finished alongside the rest of the leading contenders to retain his fifth position overall and keep hold of the white jersey for the best young rider.

Mas, who has finished second overall three times in the Vuelta, has a cushion of one minute and 37 seconds heading into Saturday's 186.8km mountain stage from La Calahorra to Collado del Alguacil.

The 31-year-old will hope to seal his first Grand Tour title when the race concludes on Sunday with a 112km stage in Granada.

title: Hunt sets sights on Lions tour after injury return
description: England scrum-half Natasha Hunt says the inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour to New Zealand - the first Test of which is exactly a year away today - is a massive motivation as she prepares to make her comeback from injury.
fullText:
England scrum-half Natasha Hunt says the inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour to New Zealand - the first Test of which is exactly a year away - is a massive motivation as she prepares to make her comeback from injury.

The 37-year-old sustained knee ligament damage during England's Six Nations opener against Ireland in April.

She was sidelined for the rest of the Red Roses' Grand-Slam winning campaign and Gloucester-Hartpury's run to the PWR semi-finals, but starts at nine in England's WXV Global Series opener against Australia in Salford on Saturday.

"I've been fortunate enough to have played in Team GB Sevens set-ups twice over," said Hunt, a veteran of the Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2021 Olympics.

"That was some of my favourite, most enjoyable rugby, just mixing cultures, everyone having a common goal and coming together really quickly to try to get something special done.

"It would be unbelievable to be involved in [the Lions tour].

"I think every player that is close to playing for their country in those four nations is thinking about it. And if they say they're not, they're lying!"

The landmark five-fixture tour begins on 4 September with a warm-up fixture against a Black Ferns XV, before the first of three Tests against New Zealand seven days later.

Coach Jo Yapp is expected to name her squad in May 2027, after the conclusion of next year's Women's Six Nations.

Hunt spent much of the past summer working with Gloucester's strength and conditioning team to rehabilitate her knee and, after seeing Lucy Packer impress in her absence, has got the nod to start against the Wallaroos.

Hunt forms a half-back partnership with Holly Aitchison. The pair first played together almost a decade ago, when Aitchison was a fast-rising teenage prospect at Litchfield Ladies.

"We played one game together - I was nine, she was 10 against Worcester and we really enjoyed it," remembers Hunt.

"She's just such an exciting rugby player. Her ability to play at the line is pretty unmatched in the game.

"The way that she can take a ball at such pace, challenge that line and then fizz a pass 20 metres... I don't think there's many people in the game that can do that."

After taking on Australia, who they beat 47-7 en route to winning the World Cup last year, England face Canada and New Zealand on the following two weekends.

The second half of the WXV Global Series takes the Red Roses across the Atlantic in October for a match against the USA and a two-Test series against Canada.

title: Alonso cannot leave F1 while uncompetitive - FIA boss
description: FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem says it would be "not acceptable" for Fernando Alonso to leave F1 while he is in an uncompetitive position.
fullText:
FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem says it would be "not acceptable" for Fernando Alonso to leave Formula 1 while he is in an uncompetitive position.

The 45-year-old two-time world champion is out of contract with Aston Martin at the end of this season and on Thursday said his decision on whether to stay in F1 would be made "not soon".

Aston Martin are 10th in the championship so far this season after producing an uncompetitive car, while engine partner Honda's power-unit is the least powerful on the grid.

Ben Sulayem, the head of motorsport's governing body, said at an event in Madrid on Friday: "There is no way we can allow Fernando to leave - Alonso, a great champion - to leave just because of the circumstances.

"That's not the way to leave the stage. He has to be successful and then he leaves whenever he wants, not because he was forced to leave because of the performance."

Lindblad crashes as Antonelli fastest in Madrid

How to follow Spanish Grand Prix on the BBC

Ben Sulayem, whose time as FIA president has been marked by controversy around issues such as removing checks and balances in the organisation's governance, said: "I will be speaking to him. I said to him, I saw him very sad, and I said, 'Fernando, I understand, it's not acceptable that you are coming to your own country and now after two times a world champion…'

"We did something earlier, in May, legally for the team towards the engine to go and improve, and then I said to him: 'I am not going to tell you what we are going to do. Please tell me what you want because you are the driver and come and tell me what do you want us to do to improve these results.'"

An FIA spokesperson said Ben Sulayem was referring to F1's additional development and upgrade opportunities (Aduo) system.

This gives engine manufacturers whose power-units are assessed to be more than 2% behind the best chances to upgrade its design.

"It is a comment about the Aduo process and that he hopes Fernando Alonso stays in the sport," the spokesperson said. "That is all."

Pressed on the fact that Ben Sulayem appeared to be suggesting he could intervene to make changes in a way that could be considered as overreaching his position as leader of an organisation that has a role to independently and objectively administer, the spokesperson said: "He is passionate about the drivers, having been one himself, and I really would not read too much into this."

title: Moroccan official told to stop making 2030 final promise
description: Morocco's prime minister tells the head of the country's football federation to stop making promises about the 2030 World Cup final, while the head of the Spanish federation says the showpiece should be played in Spain.
fullText:
Morocco's prime minister has told the head of the country's football federation to stop making promises about the 2030 World Cup final as Spain says they should stage it.

The next men's World Cup will be co-hosted by Morocco, Spain and Portugal, although the opening three matches will be played in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay to mark the competition's 100th anniversary.

While a list of host stadiums has been proposed, the line-up has yet to be finalised, as well as where the showpiece will take place.

Fouzi Lekjaa, president of the Moroccan football federation (RMFF), declared at a political party event Casablanca would have the 'honour' of hosting the game.

Fifa, world football's governing body and organisers of the World Cup, said "a decision will be made in due course".

At a rally, Morocco's prime minister Aziz Akhannouch also told Lekjaa: "Do not offer to host the big final game in Morocco while we still have not discussed the matter with our allies, Spain and Portugal."

"There should be some respect, brothers. Stop using electoral promises to pull the rug out from under us. These are huge matters. Deciding where the final will be held is a major issue."

Rafael Louzan, president of the Spanish football federation (RFEF), has previously said the final will be held in Spain, and felt their claim has been strengthened by winning the men's World Cup for the second time this summer.

"Even though no decision has been taken, I believe Spain is the place because it cannot be any other way," he told Cadena SER radio station. "As you know, we are currently world champions.

"I believe Spain's organisational capacity for major events is beyond question and that is why reality dictates that the grand final cannot and must not be held anywhere other than in Spain."

Spain beat Argentina to win this year's World Cup in July, although New Jersey was not confirmed as the host for the final until February 2024 - two years before the tournament took place.

Morocco are constructing a proposed 115,000-seat stadium, which would make it the largest football stadium in the world.

In Spain, Real Madrid's Bernabeu Stadium has recently been renovated and now holds 83,000, while the capacity at Barcelona's Spotify Camp Nou will be 105,000 once renovations there are complete.

title: England need 130 after thrilling Razaullah hitting
description: England face a chase of 130 to win the third Test after Pakistan debutant Razaullah produces some thrilling resistance on day three at Edgbaston.
fullText:
Third Rothesay Test, Edgbaston (day three of five)

Pakistan 133 (Tongue 4-42) & 449 (Masood 95, Razaullah 81, Babar 76, Awais 59)

England 453 (Brook 75, Smith 69, Lawrence 65, Gay 60, Robinson 50; Razaullah 4-148)

England face a chase of 130 to win the third Test after Pakistan debutant Razaullah produced some thrilling resistance on day three at Edgbaston.

Pakistan had battled to 318-8, still two runs behind, with potentially more than two hours of play remaining when Razaullah, the tourists' number nine, launched a sensational assault.

The 21-year-old's audacious 81 from 63 balls frazzled England and propelled Pakistan to 449. His nine sixes tied Ben Stokes' record for the number of maximums in a Test innings in England.

Razaullah shared an ninth-wicket stand of 121 with Muhammad Abbas, who whacked two sixes of his own in his 42. Finally, Razaullah was stumped off Lawrence to end the day and signal the beginning of England's chase on Saturday.

Pakistan deserved to drag the match into a weekend, restoring a modicum of pride to what has been a shambolic tour.

England might have won inside two days had it not been for bad weather on Thursday. From 55-2 overnight, 268 behind, Pakistan did not capitulate on Friday.

Shan Masood and Azan Awais extended their third-wicket stand to 125 until Awais tickled the off-spin of Dan Lawrence down the leg side for 59.

Masood added another 89 with captain Babar Azam. The left-hander was denied a century on 95 when Lawrence took a spectacular one-handed catch at gully off Gus Atkinson.

Babar was classy for his 76, yet was discomforted when England went to a short-ball plan either side of tea. His dismissal to a Josh Tongue bouncer seemed to confirm a three-day finish, but Razaullah had other ideas.

Razaullah introduces himself as Pakistan thrive in the madness

'Out of control' - Cook questions England tactics

On what could have been the final day of a disappointing series, a Test match broke out. The contest between bat and ball was even and compelling, and the Hollies Stand filled Edgbaston with an atmosphere missing from the first two days.

In their last act of a miserable tour, Pakistan showed what they are made of. Until Razaullah flayed them, England did not bowl badly - the hosts were simply met with patience, bravery and sound judgement from the touring top order.

Despite being bowled out for 133 on day one and reduced to 0-2 in their second innings, Pakistan are alive. England should win, though the tourists will have a target to defend. The run chase could be ticklish.

Razaullah was one of the seven players Pakistan drafted into the squad for this Test. He first impressed with his pace bowling in England's first innings, then provided grandstand entertainment late on Friday evening.

After a first full day in the field this series, England faded. As Razaullah and Abbas swung and swiped, England's bowlers simply could not hit the stumps. Joe Root's decision to employ Lawrence with the second new-ball was curious.

England were left frustrated and devoid of ideas. For everyone else, it was tremendous fun. Saturday might yet be something special.

Pakistan could have been humiliated in Birmingham, so the performance they produced on Friday was a staggering turnaround. This was the first time they have made more than 200 or batted more than 51 overs in the series.

At 21, Awais looks a prospect and played nicely through the off side. Masood was composed and unfortunate to miss out on a century in what is likely his final Test in the country where he went to school.

Babar showed glimpses of his class, only to lose concentration when England went to bouncers - the captain's dismissal was the first of four wickets to fall for 40 runs.

What came next was remarkable. Razaullah struck the ball clean and long. It started as freewheeling hitting and turned into a match-changing innings. He equalled the record held by New Zealand's Tim Southee for the most sixes in an innings by a Test debutant.

Atkinson was belted into the Edgbaston building site as part of three maximums in the same over, while Jofra Archer was hit back over his head for successive sixes.

Even Abbas got in on the fun. He played reverse-sweeps off Lawrence and clobbered Ollie Robinson over cow corner for two sixes.

As the light faded, it seemed as though the ninth-wicket pair might reach the close, only for Abbas to poke Tongue to point.

In a frantic finish, Razaullah cracked Lawrence for the record-equalling ninth six, drew huge cheers when he overturned being given lbw, then was stumped. He left to a rapturous ovation, a new star of Pakistan cricket.

England's attack have had it all their own way this series. Root's tactics, often criticised in his first spell as captain, have rarely been tested. Friday's chaos will bring plenty of questions for this new regime.

The hosts' efforts for the majority of the day were adequate - they were simply repelled by some quality Pakistan batting. When the ball moved, England held their length, then went to a short-ball plan at the right time and took some sharp catches.

But when Razaullah and Abbas came together, England lost the plot. The field was scattered for bouncers and, when the bowlers tried to target the stumps, they either missed the target or were met by stout Pakistan defence.

Robinson has been in the form of his life, yet was somehow ignored for the second new-ball in favour of Lawrence. Archer could not hide his frustration at the treatment he received from Razaullah, while Root briefly left the field.

The late wickets were a huge relief. England dragged themselves off the field, chastened, though still in line for a 3-0 clean sweep.

title: The ‘hand grenade’ in Gavin Newsom’s lap
description: California’s governor fought hard to keep a billionaire tax off the ballot. But he didn’t succeed — and now the campaign will test his presidential prospects.
fullText:
Gavin Newsom fought hard to keep a California billionaire tax off the ballot. Now, he's keeping his distance.

Months ago, Newsom personally lobbied the initiative's backers to withdraw the one-time levy, warning the proposal had already begun driving ultrawealthy residents and their businesses out of state. He remains one of its most prominent foes and has been kept apprised of the opposition campaign. But he is not fundraising or taking a lead role in messaging against a measure that could become an early test of his political standing and economic vision ahead of a likely presidential bid.

The calculation reflects the bind that Proposition 40 poses for Newsom. If it passes despite his early warnings, he risks looking disconnected from populist fury over inequality and President Donald Trump's health care cuts. If it fails, Newsom and his allies would be vindicated — but Democratic rivals on the left could still point to the defeat as a sign that he is overly attuned to anti-tax tech billionaires.

Now, as he enters his final campaign cycle as governor, Newsom must decide how much political capital to spend against an initiative that has cleaved California's Democratic coalition.

"It feels like a sticky wicket for him," said Jim Kessler, president of Third Way, a centrist Democratic think tank. "Newsom's a smart guy. He may have this figured all out. [But] a little hand grenade was tossed in his lap with this."

Newsom has long argued the wealth tax — a proposal to offset federal health care cuts by imposing a one-time, 5% levy on the assets of California's wealthiest residents — is the wrong solution to a real problem.

He established himself early on as its most prominent political opponent, echoing Silicon Valley rancor in assailing the proposal as an ill-conceived threat to California's economic competitiveness that would drive vital taxpayers out of state. He worked behind the scenes to derail it, encouraging groups like the California Teachers Association and Planned Parenthood to come out against the measure, while issuing a broader call to "democratize the economy" by raising taxes in other ways.

"The strategic implications of Gavin Newsom being vocally opposed to the wealth tax couldn't be bigger," said Chris Lehman, a longtime ballot initiative consultant who is not working on the wealth tax. "Everyone is dealing with the calamitous effects of wealth inequality, and this looks like a great answer, so if Gavin Newsom is saying to people, 'It looks like a good idea but it's not, and here's why,' that is strategically massively important."

But the politics have only become more fraught in the weeks since the proposal made the ballot. Proponents picked up key endorsements from the California Labor Federation and the California Democratic Party, undercutting efforts by Newsom and Democratic allies to present a united front.

"The issue's not great for him politically," said a Democratic consultant working against the wealth tax, who was granted anonymity to speak candidly. "There is a disadvantage for him with many segments of the electorate."

The California ballot initiative has quickly become a proxy for a broader Democratic fight over how aggressively to tax the ultrawealthy — a debate likely to shape the 2028 primary. Soon after the measure qualified, Newsom countered with a menu of national tax increases that could form the core of a presidential platform — an acknowledgement that Democratic voters expect their leaders to tackle widening economic inequality, even as he rejects Prop 40's approach.

"There's not going to be a single Democrat running for president in 2028 that will not have a plan to dramatically increase taxes on the most wealthy. That will be unanimous," Kessler said. "How they do it will differ."

Wealth tax proponents like Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Ro Khanna, a California progressive who is also eyeing a White House bid, have portrayed the measure as a litmus test for voters eager to see their leaders take on entrenched economic powers. Newsom's opposition could make him an easy target for the left.

"His critics, which would certainly include opponents in the presidential race, will make the charge that he turned his back on the voters suffering from income inequality and the lack of affordable health care," said Darry Sragow, a longtime Democratic consultant in California. "For his opponents, that's just lobbing it across the net. That's an easy one."

That line of attack has already begun as the wealth tax campaign plays out in the shadow of the 2028 contest. Khanna has invoked Newsom's presidential ambitions and portrayed him as part of a corrupt establishment dependent on oligarchs' campaign cash.

"They're going to put the governor's face on it, and they're going to put elected officials' face on it, and they're going to fearmonger," Khanna said at a recent campaign event.

Newsom has not been directly involved in making strategic decisions for the No side, though he has several key aides either embedded in the campaign or in regular communication with it.

"We do not suffer from lack of information about what is going on," said a Newsom adviser granted anonymity to discuss internal deliberations.

As the anti-Prop. 40 effort took shape, there was anxiety among some in the governor's orbit for not being sufficiently read in on the campaign's plans. But two people involved in the effort said those concerns have largely subsided as communication improved and the campaign's ads began to hit the airwaves.

Newsom himself may not be the most effective messenger against the tax, unlike when he led a highly partisan gerrymandering campaign last year. The first ad featured the governor but did not make him the main character. Instead, he shared the billing with a cast of opponents that included Republican governor nominee Steve Hilton, his Democratic opponent Xavier Becerra, and union foes, like teachers and firefighters, that have broad cross-party appeal.

"Our task as a campaign is to let voters know, especially Democratic voters, who's lined up against this measure," said Anthony York, a spokesperson for the opposition. "When they learn not only Governor Newsom but Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton are against it, it changes the perception of what this measure does."

Most polls have given the wealth tax at best a fragile lead, even before a deluge of opposition ads begins. The opposition effort doesn't need Newsom to raise money, as a group of billionaires led by Google co-founder Sergey Brin is pouring tens of millions of dollars into fighting the tax.

title: China’s car exports in first 8 months surpass 2025 total, as EV sales soar
description: China’s passenger car exports in the first eight months of this year already surpassed last year's total, an industry association said Thursday, though domestic sales continued to decline.  Passenger car exports in August jumped 67.1% from the year before to around 890,000 units, driven by plug-in hybrids and pure electric vehicles, according to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers (CAAM).  China exported more than 6.2 million passenger vehicles in January-August.
fullText:
HONG KONG (AP) — China's passenger car exports in the first eight months of this year already surpassed last year's total, an industry association said Thursday, though domestic sales continued to decline.

Passenger car exports in August jumped 67.1% from the year before to around 890,000 units, driven by plug-in hybrids and pure electric vehicles, according to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers (CAAM).

China exported more than 6.2 million passenger vehicles in January-August. Exports of all types of vehicles totaled 7.1 million last year, CAAM data show, including about 6 million passenger vehicles.

The world's largest car exporter is on track to achieve 50% to 70% growth in full-year passenger vehicle exports, according to S&P Global Ratings.

At home, passenger car sales fell 25.6% year-on-year in August to just below 1.5 million vehicles.

China's domestic car market is under pressure from intense competition and price wars, while the slowing economy has undermined consumer confidence.

China's car exports have been stronger than expected so far this year, helped by competitive pricing and quality, said Stephen Chan, an associate director at S&P Global Ratings.

"It's likely that strong export growth will largely mitigate the domestic weakness," he said.

Over the past few months the energy shock from the Iran war and rising fuel prices have led more drivers of gasoline and diesel-powered vehicles to shift to EVs.

Hefty tariffs have in effect kept most Chinese-made passenger cars out of the U.S. market. But China has been exporting and selling more of its vehicles to Europe, Latin America, Africa and Southeast Asia.

Chinese automakers are also setting up more factories overseas.

Weak domestic demand is increasing carmakers' incentives to redirect capacity overseas, analysts at Morgan Stanley said in a recent research note, and Chinese carmakers are increasingly moving beyond vehicle exports toward local assembly and manufacturing to ease impacts from trade barriers and reduce logistics costs.

title: FBI arrests suspect accused of paying LA homeless to forge signatures using registered voters' identities
description: James Brass allegedly ran a ballot harvesting scheme on Los Angeles' Skid Row, paying homeless people to sign petitions using stolen voter identities.
fullText:
A California man was arrested early Thursday amid allegations that he and two others paid homeless people living in Los Angeles' Skid Row neighborhood to sign petitions using the stolen identities of registered voters in an effort to qualify ballot initiatives for local elections.

James Brass, 47, a.k.a. "Lord," was taken into federal custody in Victorville, 85 miles northeast of Los Angeles, the Justice Department said. Brass and the other two defendants — Courtney Price, 49, of Jacksonville, Florida, and Jateisha Herron, 33, of Boron, California — are charged with conspiracy to commit identity fraud in furtherance of a state felony.

Brass and Price are additionally charged with identity fraud in furtherance of a state felony.

Trump Election Fraud Crackdown Lands First Arrest, Putting Longtime Critics In White House Crosshairs

"Securing American elections from criminal interference is of the upmost importance to this FBI," FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital. "For at least 6 months in 2026, these subjects were allegedly paying homeless people on Skid Row in downtown Los Angeles to sign petitions in support of ballot initiatives, all using stolen identities of registered voters."

"Election security will always be a top priority of this FBI," Patel added.

Brass allegedly orchestrated the ballot harvesting scheme through the management of a team of signature collectors, as well as collecting signatures himself, federal prosecutors said.

Ex-new Jersey Mayor, Her Husband Charged For Using Fake Ballot Signatures After She Pleaded Guilty To Dui

Price and Herron were employed by Brass, authorities said.

From February through August, the trio allegedly gathered the identities of voters from a database and handed the information to homeless people on Skid Row, a neighborhood in downtown Los Angeles that contains one of the largest concentrations of homeless people in the United States.

Former Dem Mayoral Candidate Admits Forging Voter Registration Applications

Fbi Raids Soros-backed Voter Group's Headquarters In Reported Fraud Probe

The homeless participants were allegedly paid to sign petitions in the names of the voters.

After the petitions were signed, Brass and Herron signed declarations at the bottom of the petitions, declaring that they personally witnessed the named registered voters sign the petitions and that each signature was, to the best of their knowledge, "the genuine signature of the person whose name it purports to be," federal prosecutors said.

The bogus petitions were turned in by Brass and Herron to petition coordinators. In total, authorities claim Brass was paid $41,600 from one petition management company.

Bill Essayli, first assistant U.S. attorney for the Central District of California, said the alleged conduct "undermines the confidence voters have in our election systems," adding his office "will vigorously investigate and charge anyone involved in corrupting our elections."

All three defendants face up to five years in prison per count if convicted. Brass is expected to appear in court Thursday.
